layer_b_declaration.axis: The utterance encodes that reception of authority costs the receiver's own blood
layer_b_declaration.foreclosure: The source forecloses any transfer of the sealed book without the prior slaying
layer_b_declaration.wager: The Lamb's slaughter is the price the composition stakes as the condition of worthiness
layer_b_declaration.affect: Vertiginous gravity — a weight that falls inward even as the multitude expands outward

independent_verification.recovered_law: In Text A, the Lamb's worthiness is grounded in a completed act of slaughter and redemption (ἐσφάγης καὶ ἠγόρασας — second-person singular past), so worship follows from what he has already done. In Text B, the slaughter is recast as future or contingent consequence of worthiness (ἵνα σφαγῇς, ὅτι τὸ ἀξίωμά σου ἐπέσπασεν τὴν σφαγήν), and the worship precedes the sacrifice (πρὸ τοῦ σφαγῆναι, πρὸ τοῦ τραύματος), reversing the causal direction so that dignity draws suffering rather than suffering conferring dignity.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both describe the same reversal: in the transformed text worthiness/authority causes slaughter rather than slaughter conferring worthiness/authority, i.e., the causal direction of the dependency is flipped.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final portion (5:10–11) in Text B retains the altered temporal-causal framing (ἕως ὅτου τὸ αἷμα ἐξεχύθη marking the reign as prior to or conditional on the blood-shedding), so the changed relation persists and there is no reversion to Text A's structure.

rotation.commentary: The joint that does the most work is 5:9b–5:9c: "ὅτι ἐσφάγης" (because you were slain → authority) is inverted to "ἵνα σφαγῇς, ὅτι τὸ ἀξίωμά σου ἐπέσπασεν τὴν σφαγήν" (so that you might be slain — for the worthiness drew the wound), so the royal office becomes grammatical subject of the purchase-by-blood in place of the Lamb, propagating authority-as-cause-of-slaughter through 5:8a's "πρὸ τοῦ σφαγῆναι" and 5:10a's "ἕως ὅτου τὸ αἷμα ἐξεχύθη" without ever naming the reversal.
